title: Schedule of the Seat and Cabin Extras Charging Basis — Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
A standard advance seat is free of charge on a fare brand of Air Ticket Fare Brands that includes seat selection, and is otherwise charged per traveller per segment at the standard seat rate of the brand held.

| Cabin product | Basis on which it is carried or charged |
|---|---|
| Standard advance seat | Free where the brand held includes seat selection; otherwise the standard seat rate of that brand, per traveller per segment |
| Extra-legroom seat | The extra-legroom rate of the brand held, per traveller per segment, even where standard seats are free on that brand, the two being different products |
| Priority boarding | Free where the brand held includes it; otherwise charged per traveller per segment at that brand's rate |
| Lounge access, a hot meal, an onboard wifi voucher | Included or not included by brand, and never sold separately here |
| A pet in the cabin | The pet in cabin rate of the brand held |
| An unaccompanied minor | The unaccompanied minor rate of the brand held |
| Registered special assistance | Free of charge, but only where registered at least the lead time of the brand held before departure |
| An upgrade into a higher cabin | Sold only on a brand that allows it, at that brand's co-payment per traveller per segment |

**Annotation to the seat lines.** At the seat-map release point of the brand held, counted back in hours from scheduled departure, the remaining seats are opened for free selection, and a seat taken after that point carries no charge on any brand. Worked on a hypothetical departure at 18:00 on 14 May, with an illustrative release point of 60 hours before it used only to carry the counting through: the seats open at 06:00 on 12 May, a seat taken at 07:00 on 12 May carries no charge, and a seat taken at 05:00 on 12 May is charged on the basis set out above.

**Annotation to the special assistance line.** The lead time is likewise counted back in hours from scheduled departure, and registration at the resulting instant is enough, the boundary itself satisfying the requirement. On the same hypothetical departure at 18:00 on 14 May, with an illustrative lead time of 36 hours, registration recorded at 06:00 on 13 May is registered in time and carries no charge, while registration recorded at 06:30 on 13 May is not, and the free-of-charge basis is not available for it.

**Annotation to the upgrade line.** An upgrade never converts the booking to the higher cabin's brand terms; the booking continues to be held on the brand it was sold in, and only the co-payment is taken.
